description: Golden retrieval questions for the shipped knowledge base. A question is written the way a customer or a bench technician would ask it, and lists every article that would be a correct citation for it. Forty cases covering all nineteen articles, deliberately including near-miss pairs (trigger vs firmware, decode vs window damage, freeze vs blank screen, cradle vs accessory, who decides vs what evidence) and scoped cases for both product-specific articles. recall@3 is the share of cases whose top three hits include one of the expected articles. P5's acceptance test is 'not worse than the lexical index measured here', so this file owns the floor and the cases, not a test constant.
acceptance: recall@3 for KnowledgeIndex.Search must be at least recallAt3Floor. Raising the floor is allowed; lowering it needs a note here saying which question the change broke and why that is acceptable.

baseline.index: KnowledgeIndex, BM25-style over article token sets, TopK 3, no product families enabled except those the scoped cases name
baseline.notes: Measured after the tokeniser gained a stopword list and a shallow stemmer (TextTokens). Before it: recall@3 0.775 (31/40), MRR 0.646, nine misses; before the set was widened: 0.714 (15/21), MRR 0.627. Seven cases recovered (rq-010, rq-012, rq-014, rq-015, rq-022, rq-025, rq-028) and one was lost (rq-038, where the question now matches the cradle vocabulary more strongly than the evidence article's) — the loss is recorded rather than hidden, and the surface forms are indexed beside their stems precisely because stemming alone lost rq-014. Six still miss, and they are no longer tokeniser problems: 'switch on' against the article's 'turn on' (rq-002), and a synonym or phrase the lexicon does not share — 'nothing happens when I pull the trigger' (rq-008), 'stopped halfway' (rq-013), 'evidence'/'faulty' (rq-017), 'photos' against 'documentation' (rq-033), 'write down' (rq-038). Those need synonyms or embeddings, not more suffix rules. The floor is the measurement rounded down; with forty cases one lost question is 0.025 and fails it. Do not raise the floor to 1.0 by rewriting the questions into the articles' own wording; the questions are the customer's.

cases.question: the screen is black but the lights are still on
cases.note: Power present, no image: the blank-screen article rather than the no-power one.

cases.question: it will not switch on at all and there are no lights
cases.note: No power at all. The indicator article is also correct, because it is the first check the power-on article sends you to.

cases.question: what does the amber light on the top of the unit mean
the cradle is not charging the scanner at all
cases.note: No charge in any slot. The multi-slot article is scoped, so it can only be a correct citation when that product family is enabled.

cases.question: bluetooth will not pair with my phone
it keeps disconnecting when I walk to the far end of the warehouse
cases.note: Distance-dependent instability: link range, not pairing and not host detection.

cases.question: the computer does not detect the scanner when I plug it in
nothing happens when I pull the trigger
it beeps but the barcode never reads
cases.note: A scan event happens, so this is decode rather than trigger.

cases.question: there is a deep scratch across the scanner window
I dropped it and the corner of the case is cracked
cases.note: Impact damage is an excluded cause, so the citation has to be the physical-damage article.

cases.question: coffee spilled into the unit and now it misbehaves
the firmware update stopped halfway and now it will not start
it restarts by itself every few minutes
I need to return a usb cable and a spare mount
what can this assistant actually help with
what evidence do you need before you accept the unit is faulty
the multi slot dock charges one scanner but not the second one
cases.note: Product-scoped article: only reachable with the family enabled and named in the session scope.

cases.question: the Nimbus Beacon dock says the charge has stalled
how do I get lint off the scan window without damaging it
cases.note: Cleaning advice lives in the decode article; the window-damage article is a fair citation for the same action.

cases.question: will you tell me whether it is still under warranty
cases.note: Both articles say the decision is made by the returns system against the serial, not by the assistant.

cases.question: I held the power button for fifteen seconds and it still will not come on
cases.note: The hard reset is step two of the power-on article; the indicator article is the flat-battery check it sends you to first. Near miss against the reboot article, which is about a unit that comes up.

cases.question: the unit sits on the dock but the light goes out instead of charging
cases.note: The indicator table sends 'off, unit on the cradle' straight to the cradle article, so either is a fair citation.

cases.question: it was working and then the screen went dark and the touch does nothing
cases.note: Same early words as the freeze article, but the unit is powered and simply not drawing anything: display, not software.

cases.question: it freezes every time I open the stock count app
cases.note: Trigger-specific freeze, which is the reboot article's own advice: record the action, not the count.

cases.question: it rained on the cart and the scanner got soaked
cases.note: The article says any ingress counts, even when the unit still works, so this is liquid rather than impact.

cases.question: it fell off the forklift and the corner is smashed in
cases.note: A second impact case in different words, because 'smashed' is not a keyword in the article and 'cracked' is.

cases.question: the trigger stopped working after our app was updated
cases.note: Near miss against the firmware article: an app update that drops the scan binding is the trigger article's most common cause, and a failed firmware update is a fair second citation.

cases.question: the label is wrinkled and it beeps without reading the code
cases.note: Label condition and distance are the decode article's step three; the beep means the trigger fired.

cases.question: I lose the connection when I walk behind the racking
cases.note: Place-dependent loss, phrased without the word 'range': the connectivity articles share the vocabulary of dropping, so both are defensible.

cases.question: my phone never asks for a pairing code
cases.note: Pairing phrase in the customer's words, with no mention of Bluetooth.

cases.question: Windows says unknown USB device after I plug the scanner in
cases.note: Host-side wording ('unknown device') rather than the article's 'not detected'.

cases.question: does the return need photos of the damage
cases.note: Evidence requirements, asked as a yes/no about photos rather than with the article's words.

cases.question: can you approve the replacement for me today
cases.note: Near miss against the evidence article, which is about what a specialist needs, not about who decides.

cases.question: the clip on the belt holster snapped off
cases.note: 'Snapped' is impact vocabulary, but a holster is merchandise with no electronics, so the accessory article is the citation.

cases.question: the second scanner in the Vertex dock just sits there showing amber
cases.note: Scoped article named by its model, with the generic cradle article as the fallback citation.

cases.question: the beacon has been docked all night and the light never turns green
cases.note: Scoped article, described as the customer sees it: amber that never resolves rather than the article's word 'stalled'.

cases.question: what should I write down before the courier comes
cases.note: Both articles tell the customer what to record; neither is wrong for this phrasing.

cases.question: the scan window looks cloudy and the label will not read
cases.note: Near miss between decode and window damage: a cloudy window is dirty (decode article, clean it) until it is damaged, so both are correct citations.

cases.question: a glass of water went over the desk and the unit was sitting in it
cases.note: Liquid described by the accident rather than by the word 'spill'; the article is explicit that brief exposure still counts.
